restrictions: Message B is 1,088 zero bytes: a 1,024-byte chunk and a 64-byte chunk, whose root is their parent compression with flags 12. Message A has 64 bytes: one chunk of one block, whose root compression has flags 11. Both root compressions use the IV, counter 0 and block length 64.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 1 prefix round, standard IV, chunk tree, flags and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.
Deterministic: the algorithm uses no coins and outputs the same collision on every run, so there is no failed trial and no restart.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; a straight-line program charged with 19 target compressions (the 17 chunk compressions of B and the two root compressions, which together are the complete hashes of both messages and serve the final collision check) and with memory traffic at four primitive operations per data operation.

No preprocessing, table, stored collision or nonuniform advice: every word of the output is computed by the counted program from public constants; the preprocessing and advice fields are zero-valued upper bounds because the schema cannot express log2(0).

Specific to the 1-round prefix: the identity is proved for one round only, nothing is claimed for two or more rounds (the pair has different 2-round digests), and no priority or novelty claim is made.
